How a word is rebuilt from its neighbours
"Context vector" and "output projection" sound advanced, but they are names for very plain arithmetic: a weighted average, a
, and one matrix multiplication. Six frames, each with the real numbers beside it, are enough to see all three.

every head. This is the only line in the attention block where the heads share information: if one head noticed something
is how that finding reaches the numbers the other heads produced. Without it, multi-head
attention would be four small attentions glued side by side. Section C splits one output number into the four head
contributions plus the bias, and they add up to exactly the value shown here.

A weighted average you can check with a calculator
"A word is rebuilt as a weighted average of the others" — here is that sentence as
multiplications and one addition. The top row is how much "cat_" listens to each word, the middle row is number
of each word’s value, and the bottom row multiplies them. Add the bottom row up and you get exactly the number in
the weights, the values, and their products
